title: Recover provider merge-state inconsistency without weakening closure
rawUserRequest: 发现流程问题应先改流程，再继续工单；看看什么情况，给出对策。

declaredIntent.summary: Recover a proven GitHub PR-state inconsistency with an explicit, narrowly evidenced path while preserving the normal fail-closed closure protocol.

outOfScope: Weakening or changing the normal ai-close-work-item requirement for provider state MERGED.
Deleting, force-pushing, closing, or reopening PR #470 or its branch during this corrective implementation.
Changing release tags, Releases, published assets, or candidate version state.
Resuming Python 3.11 closure, Dependabot #444, or performance Work Items before this corrective lifecycle is complete.

sources.reason: Normal closure currently correctly rejects a PR whose provider state is not MERGED before any cleanup.
Existing tests prove ordinary unmerged PRs fail closed but do not model a provider transaction that left an exact signed merge commit on base while the PR API remains OPEN.
The blocked predecessor defines the exact task identity, archived evidence, and original work branch for the recovery evidence model.
The public lifecycle contract must document the bounded exceptional recovery without normalizing provider inconsistency.

riskAssessment.reason: A provider-side partial merge can leave source history and provider PR state contradictory; any recovery must prevent accidental branch cleanup for an ordinary open PR.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized process-first correction and continuation; this Work Item implements only the guard and evidence path, not the external recovery mutation.

preReviewWarnings: The exceptional command must never be an implicit fallback from ai-close-work-item.
Every successful recovery must preserve the original open PR state in its receipt and require exact signed two-parent merge evidence plus explicit human confirmation at execution time.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Normal ai-close-work-item continues to reject every PR whose provider state is not MERGED and performs no cleanup.

A separately named recovery command rejects absent or unsigned merge evidence, wrong parent order, wrong PR branch or Head SHA, missing hosted success evidence, and missing explicit recovery confirmation before it can write a recovery receipt or request cleanup.
A valid provider-inconsistent case produces a distinct recovery receipt that records the OPEN provider state rather than claiming a normal merged PR or inventing mergedAt.
Focused regression tests cover the valid anomaly and all listed rejection cases, and lifecycle documentation in English and Japanese explains the exception and normal boundary.
Instruction-to-plan traceability records the observed #470 process defect, root cause boundary, corrective gate, and the required order before Python 3.11 closure resumes.
guidelines: Keep exceptional recovery explicit and opt-in; never silently downgrade ordinary provider MERGED verification.
Use only independently verifiable provider and Git evidence; chat text and local ancestry alone are insufficient.
Do not mutate PR #470, branches, tags, releases, or archived predecessor evidence while implementing this corrective.

intent.problem: PR #470's exact head commit was incorporated in GitHub-signed merge commit dca16f0 on origin/main, but GitHub still reports the PR OPEN with no merge event or association. Normal lifecycle closure correctly refuses cleanup, leaving the Python 3.11 Work Item blocked.
constraints: normal-close: state MERGED plus matching branch, Head SHA, merge commit, and mergedAt
exceptional-execution: separate invocation plus fresh explicit human confirmation
receipt-truth: provider-inconsistent recovery label plus observed evidence
predecessor-archive: immutable Python 3.11 Contract, Summary, and Outcome
intent.rationale: The system needs a testable, evidence-bound escape hatch for a real provider partial-success failure, while retaining the fail-closed normal path that prevents an ordinary open PR from being cleaned up.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Provider says OPEN, but an exact GitHub-verified signed merge commit on base has parents [old base, exact PR head] and hosted checks succeeded for that head.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The recovery validator accepts the evidence only when explicit recovery confirmation is supplied, then emits a recovery-specific receipt without claiming normal provider merge state.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add focused fixture-driven regression tests for exact anomaly evidence and receipt rendering.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An ordinary OPEN PR, unsigned/direct commit, wrong merge parents, wrong Head SHA, failed/missing hosted evidence, or no confirmation flag is supplied.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Recovery validation fails before receipt generation or cleanup planning.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add parameterized negative regressions that assert no recovery result is returned.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Normal ai-close-work-item is invoked for a provider OPEN PR.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The existing command remains fail closed and does not invoke the exceptional recovery path.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Preserve and run the existing normal closure rejection regression alongside the new focused suite.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user authorized process-first correction and continuation. This implementation does not execute the later provider/branch recovery mutation.

rollbackNote: Revert this corrective Work Item diff; retain the predecessor's blocked branch, PR, and archived evidence unchanged.
